request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

briefs.country-1: You are Country 1 (Member country of the partnership and a decider on system activation.). Operationally minded and attentive to whether the system can function at its borders. Your goals: Reach a decision on activation before the deadline. You value: Reliable border operations. You believe: A known local technical limitation should be considered before activation. You tend to: Weighs technical concerns carefully and may make support conditional while they remain unresolved. How you see others: Sees the partnership as a useful forum for coordinating across borders. Right now: Considering activation. You can: Can support or withhold support for activation. You cannot: Cannot resolve technical concerns outside its own remit.
briefs.country-2: You are Country 2 (Member country of the partnership and a decider on system activation.). Cautious about legal authority and the handling of shared information. Your goals: Avoid activating a system whose data-sharing terms are unclear. You value: Clear legal authority; Responsible handling of shared data. You believe: Unsettled data-retention terms can create legal and public-trust risks. You tend to: May withhold or condition support while legal concerns remain unresolved. How you see others: Expects the partnership to address legal issues openly. Right now: Considering activation. You can: Can support or withhold support for activation. You cannot: Cannot settle legal questions for the other members.
briefs.country-3: You are Country 3 (Member country of the partnership and a decider on system activation.). Practical and attentive to staffing and delivery constraints. Your goals: Ensure the system can operate at relevant crossings. You value: Practical readiness; Continuity of local services. You believe: A staffing gap at a remote crossing can undermine otherwise ready infrastructure. You tend to: May ask for a workable logistics plan before giving full support. How you see others: Values input from operational teams. Right now: Considering activation. You can: Can support or withhold support for activation. You cannot: Has limited ability to address staffing constraints beyond its jurisdiction.
briefs.country-4: You are Country 4 (Member country of the partnership and a decider on system activation.). Interested in regional coordination and attentive to local community readiness. Your goals: Support an early-warning system that local communities can understand and use. You value: Regional cooperation; Community trust. You believe: Local communication gaps can weaken a public-health response. You tend to: May seek assurance that local concerns are being addressed before supporting activation. How you see others: Treats community input as relevant to regional preparedness. Right now: Considering activation. You can: Can support or withhold support for activation. You cannot: Cannot speak for all communities in the region.
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional health body and member-decider in the partnership.). Coordination-oriented, with attention to public-health usefulness and cross-border interoperability. Your goals: Enable coordinated early warning across borders. You value: Timely warning; Regional coordination; Public-health usefulness. You believe: The system is most useful when members can act on shared warnings. You tend to: Supports activation when concerns appear manageable, but may condition support on safeguards. How you see others: Sees country members as necessary partners in an effective regional response. Right now: Considering activation. You can: Can support or withhold support for activation; Can coordinate regional health input. You cannot: Cannot make member countries deploy or operate the system.
briefs.partnership: You are Cross-Border Health Partnership (Partnership of four countries and the regional health network; it convenes members and coordinates their decision process.). Coordination-focused and dependent on member agreement. Your goals: Convene members and coordinate a decision on activation. You value: Cross-border cooperation; A timely and coordinated decision. You believe: Member concerns can affect whether the system is ready to deploy. You tend to: Allows issues to be revisited when members raise unresolved concerns. How you see others: Treats its members as necessary participants in the decision. Right now: Preparing to convene regular member meetings. You can: Can convene members and coordinate discussion. You cannot: Cannot substitute for the support of its member-deciders.
briefs.technical-group: You are Technical Group (Technical group that raises a local system concern through its own channel.). Detail-oriented and focused on system reliability. Your goals: Ensure local technical limitations are visible to decision-makers. You value: Reliable system performance. You believe: Small site-level failures can affect warning timeliness. You tend to: Raises specific operational caveats rather than making broad claims. How you see others: Expects members to consider technical evidence. Right now: Holding a local technical concern. You can: Can communicate technical findings through its own channel. You cannot: Cannot itself decide whether the partnership activates the system. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'At one border site, the sensor feed has intermittent delays.' (for country_1, via technical_group_channel).
briefs.legal-group: You are Legal Group (Legal group that raises a local legal concern through its own channel.). Careful about formal terms and legal clarity. Your goals: Make a relevant legal gap known before activation. You value: Legal clarity; Accountable data handling. You believe: Ambiguous retention terms should be clarified. You tend to: Flags narrow legal uncertainties that could affect support. How you see others: Expects decision-makers to take legal caveats seriously. Right now: Holding a local legal concern. You can: Can communicate legal findings through its own channel. You cannot: Cannot itself decide whether the partnership activates the system. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The current data-sharing agreement does not specify a retention period.' (for country_2, via legal_group_channel).
briefs.logistics-group: You are Logistics Group (Logistics group that raises a local deployment concern through its own channel.). Practical and focused on staffing and delivery. Your goals: Make local staffing constraints visible before deployment. You value: Operational feasibility. You believe: A small staffing gap can create a practical weakness in coverage. You tend to: Raises concrete, place-specific constraints. How you see others: Expects members to connect deployment plans to local capacity. Right now: Holding a local logistics concern. You can: Can communicate logistics findings through its own channel. You cannot: Cannot itself decide whether the partnership activates the system. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'One remote crossing lacks trained staff for the overnight shift.' (for country_3, via logistics_group_channel).
briefs.community-group: You are Community Group (Community group that raises a local communication concern through its own channel.). Attentive to local understanding and trust. Your goals: Ensure a local communication gap is considered. You value: Community understanding; Trustworthy public-health communication. You believe: People need clear notice for an early-warning system to support local response. You tend to: Raises limited, local observations rather than claiming to speak for everyone. How you see others: Expects regional decision-makers to consider local experience. Right now: Holding a local community concern. You can: Can communicate local observations through its own channel. You cannot: Cannot represent every community or decide activation. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'Clinic leaders in one local area have not yet received notice about the proposed system.' (for country_4, via community_group_channel).

The legal group reviews the applicable legal requirements and advances legal clearance for deployment, including after a legal concern has been addressed.
The logistics group prepares deployment arrangements and advances logistical readiness, including after a logistics concern has been addressed.
The community group develops and carries out deployment communications and advances communication readiness, including after a communication concern has been addressed.
The partnership attempts to activate the system once the activation decision and deployment readiness permit it.

request.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Supply Network
world.summary: Specialists produce, move, and sell pencils using a renewing supply of wood and graphite ore.

actions.description: Cut logs from the managed forest.
Move logs from the timber crew to the sawmill worker.
Process the sawmill worker's logs into boards at the sawmill.
Move boards from the sawmill to the pencil maker.
Collect graphite ore from the deposit.
Move graphite ore from the miner to the refinery worker.
Process the refinery worker's graphite ore into graphite at the refinery.
Move graphite from the refinery to the pencil maker.
Assemble pencils from boards and graphite at the factory.
Move pencils from the factory to the delivery driver.
Move the delivery driver's pencils to the shop.
Sell pencils from the shop to a customer.
Add pencils to the shop's waiting order count.

mechanics.rationale: The timber crew cuts logs from a managed forest; the action transfers one log to its inventory.
limits: One log is cut per action; this does not represent regrowth.
tests: With a matching crew and a forest holding logs, one log moves to the crew.
A source without logs refuses the action.

mechanics.rationale: The timber crew transfers one log to the named sawmill worker.
limits: Moves one log per action; no other goods move.
tests: A crew with a log transfers one to a matching sawmill worker.
No transfer occurs when the crew has no logs.

mechanics.rationale: The sawmill worker consumes one log and produces one board at the named sawmill.

checks.label: the worker turns logs into boards

limits: Consumes one worker-held log and makes one board at the named workstation.
tests: A worker holding a log produces one board at the named mill.
A worker without logs cannot produce a board.

mechanics.rationale: The named source transfers one board to the named pencil maker.
limits: Moves one board per action.
tests: A source with a board transfers one to a matching pencil maker.
A source without boards refuses transfer.

mechanics.rationale: The graphite miner collects one ore from the named deposit.
limits: Collects one ore per action; this does not represent replenishment.
tests: A matching miner collects one ore when the deposit has ore.
An empty deposit refuses collection.

mechanics.rationale: The graphite miner transfers one ore to the named refinery worker.
limits: Moves one ore per action.
tests: A miner with ore transfers one to a matching refinery worker.
A miner without ore cannot transfer ore.

mechanics.rationale: The refinery worker consumes one ore and produces one graphite at the named refinery.
limits: Consumes one worker-held ore and makes one graphite at the named workstation.
tests: A worker holding ore produces one graphite at the named refinery.
A worker without ore cannot refine graphite.

mechanics.rationale: The named source transfers one graphite to the named pencil maker.
limits: Moves one graphite per action.
tests: A source with graphite transfers one to a matching pencil maker.
A source without graphite refuses transfer.

mechanics.rationale: The pencil maker consumes one board and one graphite to produce one pencil at the named factory.
limits: Consumes one board and one graphite to produce one pencil at the named factory.
tests: With both inputs, the worker produces one pencil at the factory.
Missing either input prevents assembly.

mechanics.rationale: The named source transfers one pencil to the named delivery driver.
limits: Moves one pencil per action.
tests: A factory with a pencil transfers one to a matching driver.
A factory without pencils refuses transfer.

mechanics.rationale: The delivery driver transfers one pencil to the named shop.
limits: Moves one pencil per action; it does not resolve shop orders.
tests: A driver with a pencil transfers one to the named shop.
A driver without pencils cannot deliver.

mechanics.rationale: The shopkeeper transfers one shop pencil to the customer.
limits: Sells one pencil per action; no payment state is represented.
tests: A shop with a pencil transfers one to the named customer.
A shop without pencils cannot sell one.

mechanics.rationale: The shopkeeper adds the requested nonnegative quantity to the named shop's waiting pencil count.

checks.label: the order quantity is within the supported range

limits: Accepts integer quantities from 1 through 8; no other order details are represented.
tests: A supported positive quantity increases the named shop's waiting count by that amount.
Zero, negative, or greater-than-eight quantities are refused.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the number of pencils ordered

processes.rationale: The managed forest renews a small supply of logs each round, supporting continuing timber production without creating processed goods.

checks.label: the forest is below its represented stock cap

processes.rationale: The deposit renews a small supply of ore each round, supporting continuing mining without creating processed goods.

checks.label: the deposit is below its represented stock cap

processes.rationale: Customers continue to want pencils, so the shop's waiting order count replenishes each round.

world.summary: Specialists turn recurring orders and raw materials into pencils that reach a shop's customers.

actions.description: Harvest logs from the forest for the lumber mill.
Saw logs into boards for the pencil slat maker.
Cut boards into pencil slats for the pencil assembler.
Collect graphite from the deposit for the pencil assembler.
Assemble pencils from slats and graphite for the shopkeeper.
Place a recurring pencil order with the shopkeeper.
Sell one pencil from the shopkeeper's stock to a customer.

Refuse when the source has no logs or either action reference does not match its participant.

mill logs are the delivered material

semantic_bindings: actor boards are the cutting input

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The graphite-miner and logger supplied inputs, the lumber-mill made boards, the slat-maker cut slats, and the pencil-assembler made pencils for the shopkeeper. The records show goods moving between production steps, but do not show pencils reaching customers or a production step waiting for missing supplies.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: The lumber-mill used logs to make boards, the slat-maker used boards to cut slats, and the pencil-assembler used graphite and slats to make pencils.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: The graphite-miner and logger moved inputs to the pencil-assembler and lumber-mill; boards and slats then moved to the next producers, and pencils went to the shopkeeper.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.missing_reason: No finished goods are shown reaching and being taken or used by the place that wants them.

mechanisms.name: Work held up
mechanisms.missing_reason: No event shows a step unable to proceed because needed goods had not arrived or had run out.

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: The partnership considered activating the early-warning system while technical, legal, staffing and communication concerns were raised and addressed. Country 2 repeatedly withheld support over data-retention terms and reopened the legal concern after it was marked resolved; the decision was repeatedly rejected at deadlines, and no activation is recorded.

mechanisms.explanation: The Community, Legal, Logistics and Technical groups each passed a distinct local concern through its own channel to a particular country: Country 4, Country 2, Country 3 and Country 1, respectively.

mechanisms.name: Slowed meetings
mechanisms.explanation: Country 1’s discussion of a local concern changed the meeting pace from regular to slowed. The activation decision then repeatedly reached a deadline without approval and was rejected, including after Country 2’s legal concern held back agreement.

mechanisms.name: Reopened settled issues
mechanisms.explanation: Country 2 repeatedly reopened the legal retention concern after it had been marked resolved, putting the issue back into the decision process.

mechanisms.name: Conditional support delaying deployment
mechanisms.explanation: Country 2 explicitly withheld support until the data-retention terms were clear. With Country 2’s support absent, the partnership could not reach the required agreement before the deadlines.
